event.label: Still listed in 1940, the last directory transcribed so far

body.p: Prince of Wales Place is a lane off the west side of Bouverie Street, beside the Prince of Wales Hotel. In 1890 the directory lists it between No. 215 and the hotel at No. 217.
It is first listed in the directories in 1890, and in every directory after that up to 1940, the last one transcribed so far. It had at most nine listings, all of them houses.

div.head: Along the street
div.p: The directories give its corner with Bouverie Street as its only crossing (1900, 1905 and 1940). Banbridge Place is the next lane north on the same side of Bouverie Street.

div.head: Records
div.p: Every directory and electoral-roll listing for Prince of Wales Place can be browsed in search. Each directory year links to its own page from Sands & McDougall Directories.
